purpose: Bind already-published signed release facts so ceal-agent can implement its consumer cutover. This packet publishes no new capability and performs no cutover.

reading_correction.observation_reported_by_agent: Actions artifact per-platform manifest carries artifact_state: unsigned_build_candidate, therefore no signed current+rollback packet exists.
reading_correction.finding: The premise about the artifact is correct; the conclusion is not.
why: GitHub Actions artifacts are never the release. They are the unprivileged build handoff (retention-days: 1) consumed by the assemble/sign job. The signed release lives at the Ceal release origin, not on GitHub.

artifact_state is written once at compose time, before any signing step runs, and is never rewritten afterwards. The published copy of the manifest therefore still reads unsigned_build_candidate even though that exact byte sequence is cosign-signed. It is a statement about how the manifest was composed, not about whether the object is signed.

Signing is detached: for each of the 12 primary objects the release lane publishes <asset>.pem (cosign certificate) and <asset>.sig (signature). Signature state is proven by verifying those sidecars against the tag-bound OIDC identity, never by reading a field inside a manifest.
Do not treat a future manifest field as the signature check. Verify the sidecar.

reached: Fetched the live stable pointer; it names ceal-v0.69.0 with sha256sums_sha256 574586b3cc8dac46e23568b3ac674d58dcd29bef25078a9083b031cabb76defa.

Fetched SHA256SUMS, all four per-platform manifests, ceal-guide-SKILL.md, install-ceal.sh, and all 24 signature sidecars for ceal-v0.69.0 and ceal-v0.68.0, and recomputed every digest recorded below locally.

cosign verify-blob returned 'Verified OK' for SHA256SUMS and ceal-guide-SKILL.md on both tags, against certificate-identity https://github.com/corca-ai/ceal-cli/.github/workflows/ceal-release.yml@refs/tags/<tag>, issuer https://token.actions.githubusercontent.com, workflow repository corca-ai/ceal-cli, workflow ref refs/tags/<tag>.
Confirmed all 36 objects (12 primary + 12 .pem + 12 .sig) are publicly retrievable for each of the two tags.
Fetched both Gateway handoff archives and recomputed their digests; both match the tag-time gateway-handoff-lock.json.
not_reached: The four platform binaries were not downloaded, so their SHA-256 values below are quoted from the signed SHA256SUMS and the signed per-platform manifests rather than recomputed here. Their signature sidecars were fetched and digested but not verify-blob'd.
No live Gateway, provider, or Mac enrollment action was performed for this packet.

channel_semantics.current: The tag the stable pointer names. Installers resolving VERSION=stable land here.
channel_semantics.rollback: The immediately preceding published tag, kept as the deliberate fallback. It is not automatically selectable: reaching it requires an explicit pinned-tag install or a maintainer-run rollback workflow.

current.commit_subject: Release 0.69.0: the first worker build on the v0.67.0 Protocol/Client pair

release_set_root.name: SHA256SUMS
release_set_root.note: This digest is also the value carried by the stable pointer, and is the release-set identity the installer and the rollback workflow both check.

cosign.sidecar_encoding: cosign --output-certificate output, base64-encoded PEM; base64-decode before openssl/cosign consumption

certificate_validity.note: Short-lived Fulcio certificate. Verification depends on the transparency-log timestamp, not on the certificate still being inside its validity window.

regular_member_inventory.rule: Exactly these 12 primary names, each with a .pem and a .sig. Any other name under the version prefix is not a member of this release; any missing member invalidates the set.

rollback.commit_subject: Let an installed release emit its own acceptance evidence, so producing it needs no checkout

regular_member_inventory.rule: Same 12 primary names as the current envelope, each with a .pem and a .sig.

stable_and_rollback_relationship.versioned_objects_are_immutable: create-or-identical within one writer lane; a re-published byte difference fails the release job rather than overwriting
automatic_downgrade_prohibition: Release lane: before moving stable, the workflow parses the existing pointer and refuses with 'refusing to downgrade stable worker pointer' when the current tag semver-sorts above the target. A tag push can therefore never lower stable.
Installer: with CEAL_MINIMUM_VERSION set, install-ceal.sh fails with 'Latest stable Ceal worker release is older than the installed worker release' rather than installing a lower stable.
Installed worker: 'ceal update' aborts with 'The stable worker update resolved to an older release' and directs the operator to reinstall the current signed release.

Consequence for ceal-agent: rolling back is never something the stable channel does for you. Selecting ceal-v0.68.0 requires an explicit pinned-tag install of that version prefix, or a maintainer running the rollback workflow.

guarantees: Re-downloads all 12 primary objects plus both sidecars, runs sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS, and cosign-verifies every primary object against that tag's identity before the pointer moves.
Shares the concurrency group with the release lane, so rollback and a tag release cannot interleave.
maintainer_rollback_procedure.owner: ceal-cli maintainer on narnia; ceal-agent cannot and must not trigger it

guide_asset.name: ceal-guide-SKILL.md
guide_asset.warning: Byte-identical content across ceal-v0.69.0 and ceal-v0.68.0 means the guide digest alone does not identify the release. Bind the guide to a release only through that tag's SHA256SUMS, never by its own digest.

generation_dir_contents: guide/SKILL.md             (the release's ceal-guide-SKILL.md, copied under this name)
managed_release_layout.generations_are_additive: Installing a tag that already has a generation directory re-verifies every file against the signed copy and fails on any difference instead of overwriting; the previous generation is retained, so current and rollback can coexist on disk and the pointer selects between them.
managed_release_layout.guide_registration_is_not_automatic: The installer only stages guide/SKILL.md and prints its path. Nothing loads it into an agent host by itself.

mandatory: Execute the binary only through an absolute path. Resolve it to a realpath and require the realpath to be <install-dir>/.ceal-cli/worker/releases/<generation-id>/ceal-<platform>.
Require realpath(<install-dir>/.ceal-cli/worker/current) to equal that generation directory.
Require the generation directory's SHA256SUMS to be byte-identical to the SHA256SUMS this packet pins for the selected tag (digest 574586b3... for current, abad9bda... for rollback).
Require sha256(ceal-<platform>) to equal the value this packet pins for that platform and tag.
Require sha256(<generation-dir>/guide/SKILL.md) == 49f238b93dfeba041d444f83744551fee74bee1a53a1291004029b319e55541f, and require the guide the agent actually loads to be that file.

Confirm the running binary agrees: 'ceal version' must report the expected version, and 'ceal acceptance emit' reports platform, release_version, artifact_sha256, and digest_agreement measured from the running executable.

grounds_for_refusal.binary_substitution: sha256 of ceal-<platform> differs from the signed SHA256SUMS entry. The installer itself fails with 'Existing worker release generation does not match the signed release'.
grounds_for_refusal.guide_substitution: sha256 of guide/SKILL.md differs. The installer fails with 'Existing worker release generation does not match the signed guide'; the agent applies the same digest rule to whatever guide it loads.
grounds_for_refusal.symlink_tampering: The installer refuses a <install-dir>/ceal symlink whose target is not the managed literal ('Existing ceal symlink is not managed by the worker installer'), refuses a non-symlink current pointer ('Worker current pointer must be a symlink'), and refuses symlinked state directories. The binary's own findInstalledWorkerRelease refuses with 'unmanaged_release' unless basename chain is releases/worker/.ceal-cli and worker/current resolves to the generation directory.
grounds_for_refusal.source_checkout: A binary run from a build tree fails the managed-generation check ('unmanaged_release'); 'ceal update' refuses with 'This Ceal command is not running from a verified installed worker release', and 'ceal acceptance emit' refuses a build tree because it is not an installed release.
grounds_for_refusal.path_search: Nothing in this contract makes a PATH-resolved 'ceal' trustworthy. A PATH hit that does not realpath into a verified generation directory must be refused rather than probed.

embedded_provenance.statement: This section is binary-compatibility provenance for the packages compiled into the signed ceal executable. It is NOT an instruction for ceal-agent to import @corca-ai/ceal or @corca-ai/ceal-protocol. ceal-agent imports neither; it uses only the signed installed binary and the same release's guide.

packages.recorded_where: gateway-artifact-handoff.json inside the locked handoff archive, whose digest is pinned by gateway-handoff-lock.json at the release commit

rollback.note: At 0.68.0 the lock derived both tarball names from the handoff tag, so protocol and client are both 0.66.1. From 0.69.0 the lock declares the pair explicitly, which is why 0.69.0 pairs protocol 0.67.0 with client 0.69.0.

known_gap.statement: ceal-worker-release-manifest-<platform>.json records the protocol package (filename, sha256, npm_integrity, exports, producer) but records no client package section. The @corca-ai/ceal figures above are therefore not covered by the release signature directly; they are covered transitively, through gateway-handoff-lock.json at the release commit binding the archive digest, and the archive containing gateway-artifact-handoff.json.
known_gap.consequence_for_ceal_agent: Pin the client-package figures from this packet as source-owner assertion, not as signed-manifest fact, until the manifest carries a client section.
known_gap.owner: corca-ai/ceal-cli (narnia). A manifest schema addition is a release-affecting change and is not made inside this packet.

cli_execution_contract.binary: the verified installed ceal executable, invoked by absolute path
cli_execution_contract.output_rule: Every non-help result is exactly one YAML document on stdout. There is no output-format flag; do not scrape prose and do not add one.
cli_execution_contract.branching_rule: Branch on top-level 'ok'. 'ok' means the command answered what it was asked, not that the state is good. On ok:false read 'error.kind' first; that key is present on every surface.

help_is_required_and_permitted.note: The guide requires reading leaf help before supplying operands. Help reads are part of the permitted surface even though they are not in the four-command execution set below.

permitted_commands.purpose: Live capability discovery for the selected Profile. First response deliberately carries no target inventory; it states whether target selection is required and how many authorized targets exist.
permitted_commands.recovery: Configure a Gateway-issued client session, then run 'ceal capabilities' and descend to a bounded target selection.

permitted_commands.purpose: Bounded target selection for exactly one discovered capability.
constraints: Always a live query; never served from the discovery cache, and the catalog-only cache flag is rejected here.
Follow target_catalog.next_cursor only with the same capability id. Never construct, decode, or reuse a cursor.
When the Gateway answers target_catalog.selection_required with no targets and no cursor, follow next_action instead of assuming a page exists.
permitted_commands.recovery: Run 'ceal capabilities' to re-read current capability ids, re-select for that same capability, and continue one page only with the returned target_catalog.next_cursor.

permitted_commands.purpose: Invoke one discovered capability against one selected target ref.
permitted_commands.effect: read_only  (the command's own declared effect; the *capability* declares its own effect, and a write capability must declare effect: write plus its write contract)

result_shape.data: capability payload, present when the Gateway returned one
result_shape.error: present when ok is false: { kind, message, next_action, [retryable], [retry_after_ms] }

permitted_commands.input_rule: key=value operands are capability inputs governed by the capability's discovered input contract. Do not put agent-side bookkeeping in them.

permitted_commands.purpose: Read the caller's safe Gateway audit receipt for one audited outcome, including a rejected one.
permitted_commands.returns: ceal.gateway_audit_event.v1 events carrying request_id, profile_ref, membership_ref, membership_revision, registration_ref, client_ref, client_revision, subject_ref, instance_ref, occurred_at, operation, auth_decision, policy_decision, outcome, error_code, grant_snapshot
permitted_commands.recovery: Use the receipt.request_ref a 'ceal call' returned; while no audited outcome exists for it the Gateway answers 'audit_event_not_found'.

exit_codes.0: ok:true. Success of the command, not proof of an external action.
exit_codes.2: Client-side rejection before or instead of a Gateway request: invalid_argument / usage / unparsable operands.
exit_codes.3: Everything else that fails: Gateway failure, authorization denial, session unavailability, unread audit, unknown outcome, unexpected_failure.

exit_and_error_taxonomy.agreement_rule: ok:false never accompanies exit 0; the guide states ok agrees with the exit code, and every error emitter in the worker returns 2 or 3.

denial: authorization_denied  (status: blocked; the surfaced kind for a Gateway policy denial)

exit_and_error_taxonomy.retry_after_ms: Present only when the Gateway supplied it. Absence means the Gateway named no wait; do not substitute a default and do not pace against a zero.

write_unknown_outcome_recovery_rule.trigger: receipt.evidence is 'outcome_unknown' (transport failure after the request reference was allocated), or 'readback_unavailable' (Gateway returned a result whose audit event was not read back).
mandatory_sequence: Do NOT re-run the same call. For any capability whose effect is not 'read', the worker states this explicitly: 'Do not repeat this call yet; its provider outcome is unknown.'
After a short wait run 'ceal receipt show <request-ref>'.

audit_event_not_found means no audited outcome exists yet; retry the readback. A reference that never gains an audited outcome is one the Gateway never recorded, so the call did not reach provider execution.
Only an audited outcome permits a completion claim. Exit code 0 alone never proves an external action.

If the same intended write must eventually be re-attempted, keep one stable idempotency key for one intended effect. A different key for the same effect is a second write; idempotency_conflict means the key names a different governed write.
prohibited: retrying with a new idempotency key to 'get past' an unknown outcome
claiming delivery from a non-error exit
issuing a second call that makes a retry look like a new request

confirmed_prohibited: ceal session enroll   (local_write; consumes a one-time device-enrollment code through a protected input path — an operator/human action)
ceal session logout   (local_write; revokes the Gateway session and deletes local state)
ceal session          (bare form is local_write in the command table)
ceal update           (local_write; replaces the installed generation and moves the current pointer — release selection belongs to the operator, not the agent)
ceal guide register claude   (both local_write; they link the guide into an agent host's skill directory)
commands_ceal_agent_must_never_execute.no_such_command: There is no 'ceal login'. The command set is exactly: version, commands, update, guide, capabilities, session, call, receipt, observe, acceptance.
also_out_of_scope_for_the_agent: ceal observe    (starts a local HTTP observer; read_only but not part of the consumption contract)
ceal acceptance emit  (read_only; maintainer evidence path, run by an operator)
cealctl in any form  (operator control plane; a personal client host must not install or invoke it)

provenance_seam.question: Is there a supported contract that deterministically binds an Agent lease/event/requester to a 'ceal call' inside the Gateway audit event?
provenance_seam.answer: Partial. A deterministic call-to-audit-event binding exists. An Agent-side lease/event/requester identity reaching the Gateway audit event does NOT exist.

what_exists_today.format: ceal:<uuid-v4>:call  (the worker generates the uuid with crypto.randomUUID at invocation; discovery and readback derive sibling ids with :discover / :handshake / :readback suffixes)
what_exists_today.returned_in: ceal.result.v2 -> receipt.request_ref, on success and on failure alike, including the outcome_unknown case
what_exists_today.observed_evidence: docs/acceptance/ceal-v0.69.0/linux-amd64.yaml: request_ref ceal:d5bb761f-3054-41bc-9820-9861a0953839:call appears verbatim as request_id in the audit event ref gateway-audit:e0d643f6-e28c-4778-87c7-9df89a11d16b, readback_status verified.
what_exists_today.usable_pattern_for_ceal_agent: Record the returned request_ref against the Agent's own lease/event id in the Agent's store, then prove the Gateway side with 'ceal receipt show <request-ref>'. This is a post-hoc, agent-asserted join: the Gateway never learns the lease id, so the join is only as trustworthy as the Agent's own log.

what_does_not_exist: No CLI option carries an Agent lease, event, requester, or run identifier. 'ceal call' accepts only <capability-id>, --target, --profile, and capability key=value operands.
No environment variable does it either. The worker reads exactly one env var, CEAL_DISCOVERY_CACHE_TTL_MS.
The request_ref cannot be supplied or pre-declared by the caller, so the Agent cannot register the identifier in its lease log *before* the call. Binding is therefore only ever after-the-fact.
ceal.gateway_audit_event.v1 has no field for a client-asserted provenance object.
The local 'ceal observe' / agent-audit surface reads local agent transcripts only. It never reaches the Gateway and is not a provenance seam.
provenance_seam.explicitly_not_proposed: Smuggling provenance into capability key=value input. Capability inputs are governed by the capability's own contract, are forwarded toward connectors and providers, and are the wrong trust domain for caller-asserted identity. This packet does not propose it and ceal-cli would not accept it as the seam.

proposed_change.status: proposal only; nothing here is implemented, agreed, or scheduled
proposed_change.requires: coordinated change across corca-ai/ceal (protocol + Gateway audit projection, owned by vinc) and corca-ai/ceal-cli (worker CLI, owned by narnia). Neither lane can land it alone.
proposed_change.wire_impact: Protocol wire version must move from 1.3.0 to 1.4.0, with the field optional so a 1.3.0 Gateway still answers a 1.4.0 client.

part_a_protocol.carried_on: the capability-call request envelope, as a sibling of request_id — NOT inside capability input

fields.name: runtime
fields.constraint: enum-like short token, e.g. ceal-agent; max 64 chars, [A-Za-z0-9._-]

fields.name: requester_ref
fields.constraint: opaque, max 128 chars, same charset; the Agent's own notion of who asked, never a credential or an email

invariants: Client-asserted, never authenticated by the Gateway. It must be stored and returned marked as such.
Never forwarded to a connector or provider.
Rejected with invalid_arguments on charset/length violation rather than truncated.

changes: Persist the object on the audit event as ceal.gateway_audit_event.v1 -> request_provenance, with an explicit trust marker, e.g. request_provenance.assertion: client_asserted_unverified.
Return it through the receipt readback so 'ceal receipt show' can prove the binding from the Gateway side rather than only from the Agent's log.
Add it to the receipt projection allow-list explicitly. This interacts with the open ceal-cli debt that the acceptance record's receipt branch is currently pass-through rather than allow-listed.

Add first-class options to 'ceal call': --agent-runtime <token>, --agent-lease <opaque>, --agent-event <opaque>, --requester <opaque>. Validate locally against the same charset/length bounds and fail with exit 2 / invalid_argument before any Gateway request.
Emit them only as ceal.request_provenance.v1 on the request envelope; never merge them into capability input.
Echo the accepted object back in ceal.result.v2 under a new 'provenance' block so the Agent can confirm what was sent without a readback.

Optionally accept --request-ref ceal:<uuid> so the Agent can pre-register the correlation key in its lease log before the call, turning the binding from post-hoc into pre-declared. This requires the Gateway to reject a duplicate request id rather than silently aliasing it, and must stay separate from capability idempotency keys.

proposed_change.minimum_useful_subset: If only one thing lands, land --agent-lease + request_provenance.lease_ref + Gateway persistence and receipt return. That alone makes the Agent-to-audit join verifiable from the Gateway side instead of only from the Agent's own log.

non_claims: This packet does not perform ceal-agent selection, installation, apply, or cutover. It returns already-published facts for ceal-agent to pin and act on.
This packet contains no live Gateway, provider, or Mac enrollment proof.

Without a signed current+rollback envelope, the ceal-v0.69.0 GitHub Actions build artifact alone cannot activate anything: it is the pre-signing unprivileged handoff, retained for one day, and it carries no cosign certificate or signature.

artifact_state: unsigned_build_candidate inside a per-platform manifest is a compose-time self-description that is never rewritten. It is not evidence that the published object is unsigned, and it is not the signature check.
The four platform binaries were not downloaded while assembling this packet. Their digests are quoted from the signed SHA256SUMS and the signed per-platform manifests, and were not recomputed here.

Signature verification performed here covers SHA256SUMS and ceal-guide-SKILL.md on both tags. The remaining primary objects' sidecars were confirmed present and digested, not verify-blob'd; the release lane verified all 12 at publish time.

The @corca-ai/ceal client-package figures are not carried by the signed release manifest. They are covered transitively via the release-commit lock and the handoff archive digest, and are asserted here by the source owner.

Installed-and-live acceptance evidence exists for linux-amd64 only (docs/acceptance/ceal-v0.69.0/linux-amd64.yaml). darwin-amd64 and darwin-arm64 are built, signed, and published, but no install-plus-session evidence exists for either. Do not read a published darwin binary as a proven darwin install path.
protocol-vendor-pin.json records an identity only. It reaches no remote and proves nothing about the live corca-ai/ceal repository.
This packet authorizes no tag, no push, no publish, and no Gateway write.

provenance_of_this_packet.if_this_packet_and_the_origin_disagree: The origin wins. Re-fetch SHA256SUMS for the tag, cosign-verify it against that tag's identity, and treat this packet as stale.
